glance.summary: Anthropic is reportedly valued at $1.5 trillion following its latest share pricing.
Nvidia has stopped selling its advanced AI chips to China.
Disney is testing new animatronics that use AI to interact with park guests.
Snapchat now allows developers to build AR Lenses using AI assistants.

big_pour.headline: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 per share
big_pour.summary: Anthropic has reportedly priced its IPO at $83 a share, exceeding its projected range. This valuation places the company at $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis.
big_pour.why: This massive valuation signals how much investors believe in the future of AI companies.

explain.kid: A big company called Anthropic is now worth a huge amount of money, more than almost anyone expected.
explain.pm: Anthropic's IPO pricing at $83 per share reflects a $1.5 trillion valuation, highlighting significant market confidence in its long-term growth.
explain.engineer: The fully diluted valuation of $1.5 trillion, based on an $83 share price, sets a new benchmark for frontier model labs.

big_pour.headline: Nvidia halts advanced chip sales to China
big_pour.summary: Nvidia has stopped shipping its advanced AI chips to China. This decision reverses previous approvals granted by the White House last year.

big_pour.headline: Disney animatronics get an AI upgrade
big_pour.summary: Walt Disney Imagineering is testing three new Audio-Animatronic prototypes. Unlike previous versions that relied on predefined movements, these characters use AI to interact with guests.

office_blend.headline: Stretto uses AI voice for bankruptcy intake
office_blend.summary: Stretto replaced its web-form lead capture with an AI voice agent named Tara. The agent conducts bankruptcy intake interviews by phone to qualify leads.

office_blend.headline: Social Department builds AI video discovery
office_blend.summary: Social Department built a tool called QuickSearch that allows users to find specific scenes, lines, and frames across large video libraries using AI queries.

still_roasting.summary: Will Wright is developing a simulation called MyMems that uses AI to mine content from a user's personal memories.

quick_sips.summary: Snapchat now lets developers use AI assistants to build AR Lenses by describing them in plain language.
Google's AI feature in Search now includes a temporary mode that does not save conversations to search history.
Citi has stopped supporting personal finance AI agents, warning customers they are responsible if they get hacked.

stories.label: Bug fix pilot
stories.headline: GitHub and Microsoft automate open source fixes
stories.summary: In the Codename MDASH pilot, Microsoft and GitHub used AI to turn raw findings into 99 reports with suggested fixes for open source projects.

stories.label: Open standard
stories.headline: Agent Host Protocol keeps sessions synced
stories.summary: The new open Agent Host Protocol allows AI agent sessions to remain accessible across different editors, apps, phones, and the cloud.

concept.explanation: An open standard designed to keep AI agent sessions accessible and synced across various devices, including editors, apps, phones, and the cloud.

long_read.headline: Inference engineering for software engineers
long_read.summary: This newsletter recommends a deep dive into the practical challenges of inference engineering, including model selection, caching, and managing dedicated GPUs.

sign_off: That's the last sip. See you next morning.

word.definition: When a system's quality changes over time because the model, the data, or the users' requests change, even though your code didn't.
word.heard: "Evals dropped 6 points after the provider updated the model. Drift."
word.analogy: Like the same recipe tasting different when the bean supplier changes.
